newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat closes higher on corn/soybean gains.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat closes higher on corn/soybean gains.

text.p: CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed higher on gains in corn and soybeans, traders said.
Concerns about renewed forecasts for drier weather in portions of the U.S. Midwest corn/soybean growing region led to the surge in corn and bean futures, they said.
"Wheat is going along for the ride right now," a trader said.
Gains in wheat continued to be checked by a large U.S. hard red winter wheat crop being harvested this year in the U.S. Great Plains and in the eastern U.S. soft red winter region.
Commercial selling, tied to hedge selling, was noted with Cargill Inc selling one half million bushels of September and nearly one million bushels of December, traders said.
Prudential Securities bought one million bushels of September, traders said.
Wheat closed unchanged to seven cents per bushel higher, with July up 3-1/2 at $3.28-1/2. September was up 4-1/4 cents at $3.36.

In spread dealings, LFG Futures did one-half million bushels of March/December at 10-1/2 cents premium March, and USA Trading did one half million March/December at 10-1/2 cents premium March, traders said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 13,000 contracts, below the 15,979 traded Thursday.
In wheat options, Tenco Inc bought 400 September $3.30 puts at 7-3/4 cents, Smith Barney sold 200 March $4.10 calls at 11 cents and bought 150 September $4.00 puts at 65 cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 4,500 contracts, below the 5,035 traded Thursday.
